records.text: Jeffrey Epstein had a notorious fight with Harvey Weinstein shortly before Weinstein's downfall.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: He was working with Weinstein. He had some notorious fight with Harvey Weinstein right before Harvey went down.

verification.notes: A lawyer for Epstein accusers publicly reported that Epstein expelled Weinstein from his home and that the two fell out over Weinstein's aggressive treatment of a young woman. That supports a serious dispute, but reliable reporting does not establish that it was broadly notorious at the time or precisely 'shortly before' Weinstein's 2017 downfall.

records.text: Harvey Weinstein should not currently be in prison.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: know what I'm saying so we were this very unlikely duo and I thought he was guilty I thought there had to have been some guilt I mean there were so many women that were coming out but this is how the media is effective at psychology is that they know if they say something over and over again it becomes true and actually I realized I didn't know anything about the case and when I took a look at it I was shocked there is no question that Harvey Weinstein should not be in prison right now and that

verification.notes: Treated as a claim that Weinstein lacks a valid legal basis for imprisonment, it is contradicted by current court records: a New York jury convicted him again in 2025, and a California appellate court upheld his rape and sexual-assault convictions in 2026 while ordering resentencing. The moral word 'should' is opinion, but the implied wrongful-custody premise is false on the current judgments.

verification.notes: The claim is an undefined generalization about the entire court system: no jurisdiction, court, actor, corrupt act, or period is specified. Individual misconduct cases cannot verify the universal accusation, and no single current source can adjudicate it as phrased.
